newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Carriers introduce rates increases ex-Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Carriers introduce rates increases ex-Amsterdam.

text.p: Cathay Pacific will be one of the carriers introducing rates increases ex-Amsterdam from March 1, its Dutch cargo manager, Achim van der Graaff, said.
Depending on destination, the increases would vary from five to 15 Dutch cents, he added.
The airline implemented a ten Dutch cents increase in December last year on perishables and general cargo, although it did not introduce a fuel surcharge like most carriers in the Dutch market.

Japan Airlines will introduce a rise on April 1, depending on destination, of between two and five percent, a cargo spokesman said. This followed a similar increase in January this year, although JAL was another carrier that steered clear of adding a fuel surcharge.
Air India is also considering rates rises ex-Amsterdam to the Indian sub-continent, said the airline's cargo manager, Herman Eikema.

Expected in April, the increases are likely to be in line with those announced by Dutch carrier, KLM and Germany's Lufthansa, he said. KLM Cargo announced increases of between 20 to 30 percent from March 1 from Amsterdam to the Indian sub-continent.
